quests.question: The media ___ often accused of sensationalism.
quests.hint: 'Media' is the plural of 'medium' - it traditionally takes a plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'Media' is the plural form of 'medium'. In careful formal writing, 'the media are' is the traditional choice, treating media as multiple outlets.

quests.question: The curriculum at this school ___ designed around real-world skills.
quests.hint: 'Curriculum' is singular - 'curricula' would be plural.
quests.explanation: 'Curriculum' is singular (the plural is 'curricula'). 'The curriculum is designed around real-world skills' - singular verb for a singular noun.

quests.question: The curricula at this school ___ designed around real-world skills.
quests.hint: 'Curricula' is the plural of 'curriculum' - it takes a plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'Curricula' is the plural form of 'curriculum'. 'The curricula are designed around real-world skills' - plural verb for this irregular plural.

quests.question: The index of consumer prices ___ fallen for the third consecutive month.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the index' (singular) - all other words are modifiers.
quests.explanation: 'The index' is the singular subject; 'of consumer prices' is a modifier. 'The index has fallen' - singular verb.

quests.question: The indices of consumer prices in all three countries ___ fallen.
quests.hint: 'Indices' is the plural of 'index' - it takes a plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'Indices' is the plural form of 'index'. 'The indices have fallen' - plural verb for this irregular plural.

quests.question: The datum collected from the first sensor ___ corrupted.
quests.hint: 'Datum' is the rarely used singular of 'data' - singular verb.
quests.explanation: 'Datum' is the singular form of 'data'. When referring to one single data point, 'the datum was corrupted' uses the singular verb.

quests.question: A growing body of research ___ that regular exercise improves mood.
quests.hint: The subject is 'a growing body of research' (singular) - one body of evidence.
quests.explanation: 'A growing body of research' is singular - 'body' is the head noun and is singular. 'A growing body of research suggests' - singular verb.

quests.question: Growing bodies of research from multiple countries ___ that exercise improves mood.
quests.hint: 'Bodies of research' is plural - 'bodies' is the head noun.
quests.explanation: 'Bodies of research' is plural - 'bodies' is the head noun and is plural. 'Growing bodies of research suggest' - plural verb.

quests.question: The team of experts appointed to review the case ___ reported its findings.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the team' (singular collective acting as one unit).
quests.explanation: 'The team of experts' is a singular collective noun acting as one body. 'The team has reported its findings' - singular verb and singular pronoun 'its'.

quests.question: A number of experts appointed to review the case ___ raised serious concerns.
quests.hint: 'A number of experts' means 'several experts' - plural verb.
quests.explanation: 'A number of experts' means 'several experts' and takes a plural verb. 'A number of experts have raised serious concerns' - contrast with 'the team has'.

quests.question: The evidence gathered from multiple sources ___ a consistent picture.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the evidence' (uncountable, singular) - prepositional phrase is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The evidence' is the subject; it is uncountable and singular. 'The evidence gathered from multiple sources paints a consistent picture' - singular verb.

quests.question: The findings gathered from multiple sources ___ a consistent picture.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the findings' (plural) - prepositional phrase is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The findings' is the plural subject; 'gathered from multiple sources' is a modifier. 'The findings paint a consistent picture' - plural verb.

quests.question: The lack of clear leadership and direction ___ affecting the team's morale.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the lack' (singular) - the 'and' connects two modifiers, not two subjects.
quests.explanation: 'The lack' is the singular subject; 'of clear leadership and direction' is a compound modifier showing what is lacking. 'The lack is affecting the team's morale'.

quests.question: The absence of clear policies ___ contributing to widespread confusion.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the absence' (singular) - 'of clear policies' is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The absence' is singular; 'of clear policies' tells us what is absent. 'The absence is contributing to confusion' - singular verb.

quests.question: The presence of both domestic and international investors ___ changed the market.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the presence' (singular) - 'of both domestic and international investors' is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The presence' is the singular subject; 'of both domestic and international investors' is a complex modifier. 'The presence has changed the market' - singular verb.

quests.question: The acceleration of developments in artificial intelligence ___ remarkable.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the acceleration' (singular) - all other words are modifiers.
quests.explanation: 'The acceleration' is the singular subject; the rest of the phrase describes what is accelerating. 'The acceleration has been remarkable'.

quests.question: The developments in artificial intelligence over the past decade ___ remarkable.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the developments' (plural) - prepositional phrase is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The developments' is the plural subject; 'in artificial intelligence over the past decade' is a modifier. 'The developments have been remarkable'.

quests.question: The complexity of the challenges facing modern governments ___ often underestimated.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the complexity' (singular) - the long modifier doesn't change that.
quests.explanation: 'The complexity' is the singular subject. Even a long modifier ('of the challenges facing modern governments') doesn't change the subject. 'The complexity is often underestimated'.

quests.question: The challenges facing modern governments ___ often underestimated.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the challenges' (plural) - 'facing modern governments' is a participial modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The challenges' is the plural subject; 'facing modern governments' is a participial modifier. 'The challenges are often underestimated'.

quests.question: A significant proportion of the population ___ now working remotely.
quests.hint: 'A significant proportion of the population' - 'population' is singular, so the verb is singular.
quests.explanation: 'The population' is a singular collective noun. When 'a proportion of' precedes a singular noun, the verb is singular: 'a significant proportion of the population is working remotely'.

quests.question: A significant proportion of workers ___ now working remotely.
quests.hint: 'A significant proportion of workers' - 'workers' is countable and plural, so the verb is plural.
quests.explanation: When 'a proportion of' precedes a countable plural noun like 'workers', the verb is plural: 'a significant proportion of workers are now working remotely'.

quests.question: The question of who ___ responsible for the decision remains unresolved.
quests.hint: Inside the embedded 'who' clause, 'who' is singular in this context.
quests.explanation: Inside the embedded clause 'who is responsible for the decision', 'who' refers to one party or person and takes a singular verb: 'is responsible'.

quests.question: The question of which policies ___ most effective remains open.
quests.hint: Inside the embedded 'which' clause, 'policies' is plural.
quests.explanation: Inside the embedded clause, the subject is 'which policies', where 'policies' is plural. The verb inside is 'are': 'which policies are most effective'.

quests.question: The issue of whether existing frameworks ___ adequate is central to the debate.
quests.hint: Inside the embedded 'whether' clause, 'existing frameworks' is plural.
quests.explanation: Inside the embedded clause, the subject is 'existing frameworks', which is plural. The verb inside is 'are': 'whether existing frameworks are adequate'.

quests.question: One of the key questions that ___ to be answered is how to fund the project.
quests.hint: The main verb agrees with 'one' (singular) - not 'questions'.
quests.explanation: The main subject is 'one', which is always singular. The relative clause 'that remains to be answered' contains 'that' referring to 'questions', but the main verb is controlled by 'one': 'one remains'.

quests.question: The ones who ___ selected will be notified by email.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'who' refers to 'the ones' (plural).
quests.explanation: 'Who' refers to 'the ones', which is plural. The verb inside the relative clause is 'were': 'who were selected'.

quests.question: All of the feedback that ___ received has been positive.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'that' refers to 'all of the feedback' - 'feedback' is uncountable (singular).
quests.explanation: 'Feedback' is uncountable and therefore singular. 'That was received' - singular verb inside the relative clause, because 'feedback' is the antecedent.

quests.question: The implications of this finding for our understanding of the disease ___ far-reaching.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the implications' (plural) - everything else is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The implications' is the plural subject. The long modifier ('of this finding for our understanding of the disease') describes them but doesn't change the agreement. 'The implications are far-reaching'.

quests.question: The implication of this finding for our understanding of the disease ___ far-reaching.
quests.hint: The subject is 'the implication' (singular) - everything else is a modifier.
quests.explanation: 'The implication' is the singular subject. The modifier ('of this finding for our understanding of the disease') describes it. 'The implication is far-reaching'.

quests.question: The underlying assumption on which these arguments ___ based has been challenged.
quests.hint: Inside the relative clause, 'which' refers to 'these arguments' (plural).
quests.explanation: Inside the relative clause 'on which these arguments are based', 'which' refers to 'these arguments', which is plural. The verb inside is 'are'.
